text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday, prepared for Reuters by the Estonian news agency, ETA. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Eesti Telefon plans to raise tariffs 12 percent from May 1, company director said.
- Tax burden will remain on the current level, Prime Minister Mart Siimann promised at a press conference yesterday.
- Pala council sought to replace the school-bus that was destroyed in a tragic accident with eight victims, but was cheated and sold an old vehicle.
- Protective customs tariffs slow down Estonia's progress towards the European Union membership, opposition Pro Partia and Rightwing say in their letter to the prime minister.
- Economy ministry specialists hope to conclude this spring a survey for opening a modern cellulose plant in Estonia.

- The mayor of the southern town of Tartu Tonis Lukas calls in an interview for cooperation in the city in order to preserve stability and is convinced that a no-confidence motion against him will fail.

- NATO plans intensive talks with the countries not admitted into the alliance in the first round, ambassador of the United States to NATO Robert Hunter yesterday said at a press conference in Tallinn.
- If it were for France to decide, Estonia would be admitted to the European Union immediately, the French Ambassador to Estonia Jacques Faure said.
- The police prefect of the eastern town of Narva Rein Laid presented a letter of resignation.
- Kalev confectionery intends to improve its positions in Russia by selling 27 percent of its shares to a Russian company and acquiring 50 percent of the shares of a package factory in Moscow.
